frameworks.name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A 10-stage diagnostic framework covering business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) that identifies where a company is stuck and prescribes next actions.

frameworks.name: Freedom vs. Optionality Model
frameworks.definition: The shift from passive freedom (all time back but no engagement) to active optionality (choice to engage in meaningful work), achieved through building capital and systems that create choice rather than forced outsourcing.

claims.text: Passive freedom—outsourcing all activities and buying back time—leads to boredom and dissatisfaction; what founders actually optimize for is optionality: the ability to choose meaningful work rather than being forced into work by financial necessity.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder or business owner who has achieved financial liquidity
claims.mechanism: Freedom without engagement options leaves the mind unstimulated; optionality enables choice of high-engagement activities that provide fulfillment.
bounded_by: Applies to founders with sufficient capital to exit; does not apply to founders early in business building without optionality

claims.text: The happiest periods in a founder's journey occur during active building and company scaling—not during periods of passive ownership or financial freedom—because building provides engagement, challenge, and identity alignment.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder with capital and active scaling experience
claims.mechanism: Building activities provide measurable progress, team interaction, and identity-driven fulfillment; passive ownership removes these engagement drivers.
bounded_by: Does not apply to founders who derive fulfillment from leisure or low-intensity work

claims.text: Alex Hormozi (2021) transitioned from passive ownership to active recruitment and team building at Acquisition.com, conducting 2 days per week of interviews to build a core team, marking a shift from financial optionality exercised as inactivity to optionality exercised as choice.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: post-acquisition, founder with sufficient capital to choose projects
claims.mechanism: Founder capital allows re-entry into building without financial desperation; structured interview cadence (2 days/week) enables systematic team building at scale.

claims.text: In 2021, Alex Hormozi sold three majority holdings (Allen, Prestige Labs, Gemwatch) and maintains current positions as minority holdings in the 20-33% ownership band, allowing capital redeployment into Acquisition.com without forced scaling pressure.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder with multiple exits and liquidity events

claims.text: The $100 Million Scaling Roadmap identifies 10 distinct growth stages at which businesses encounter predictable bottlenecks; the framework maps each bottleneck to specific interventions across 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Systematic analysis of portfolio data enables prescriptive stage-gated interventions; standardizing solutions across functions prevents single-domain optimization that creates downstream constraints.

examples.text: In 2021, Alex Hormozi took a passive seat in business operations while his CFO led acquisition activities for the three majority companies, allowing him to avoid hard scaling commitments on Acquisition.com until those exits were complete. Upon completion of the exits, he re-engaged actively, beginning daily interview-heavy recruitment to build the core Acquisition.com team, which he describes as making him 'happy as fuck' despite being objectively harder work than passive ownership.

Hormozi's portfolio spans majority holdings (pre-2021: Allen, Prestige Labs, Gemwatch) exited through sale, and current minority positions maintained in the 20-33% band. The structure of holding minority positions allows him to participate in upside without day-to-day operational burden, creating a capital base that enables his choice to re-engage in active building at Acquisition.com.

practices.text: When scaling a business, systematically diagnose which of the 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) is the binding constraint at your revenue stage, then deploy standardized solutions from the $100 Million Scaling Roadmap.

Allocate significant founder time (2 days per week minimum) to recruiting and core team building when entering a new scaling phase, prioritizing leadership-layer hires that enable leverage over day-to-day execution.
